ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r7.claim: The Qur’an’s fleeing audience has an indicated underlying motive; the Prophet should ignore them and only remind them, while benefit is reserved for those God’s laws make receptive.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p58/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p58/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p58/r3.claim: Qaswarah means lion; frightened asses and zebras flee its roar, illustrating disbelievers' evasive terror and refusal to hear the reminder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p58/r3.anchor: At the slightest of sounds, they dart away as if a lion has actually come near them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r7.speaker: ابن كيسان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r7.claim: Ibn Kaysān says qaswarah means archers or hunters; another group of lexicographers says it means a lion, while other reports give strong men or the darkness at the start of night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r7.anchor: القسورة: الرماة والصيادون، قاله ابن كيسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r8.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r8.claim: The lion interpretation is supported by a poetic simile, while Labīd's verse supports the interpretation of strong men or hunters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r8.anchor: أو الأسد، قاله جماعة من اللغويين، قال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r9.speaker: ابن الأعرابي وثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r9.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Thaʿlab say qaswarah is the darkness of the beginning of night, not its end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r9.anchor: أو ظلمة أول الليل لا ظلمة آخره، قاله ابن الأعرابي وثعلب

MUQATIL:74:34-52/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:34-52/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:34-52/r9.claim: Qaswara means archers; another reported explanation is a lion.
MUQATIL:74:34-52/r9.anchor: { فرت من قسورة } [آية: 51] يعني الرماة وقالوا الأسد

THALABI:v10p77#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p77#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p77#2/r8.claim: They interpret qaswara as archers; this is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas and Abu Musa al-Ashari.
THALABI:v10p77#2/r8.anchor: فرت من قسورة اختلفوا فيه فقال مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وابن كيسان: هم الرماة

THALABI:v10p77#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p77#2/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p77#2/r9.claim: Said Jubayr interprets qaswara as hunters, also reported from Ibn Abbas.
THALABI:v10p77#2/r9.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هم القناص وهي رواية عطية عن ابن عباس

THALABI:v10p77#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p77#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p77#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas explains qaswara as groups of men.
THALABI:v10p77#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس: فرت من قسورة قال: عصب الرجال

THALABI:v10p78/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p78/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p78/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says qaswara is a group of men; a pre-Islamic woman's verse uses the word for the people of the qaswara.
THALABI:v10p78/r1.anchor: سئل ابن عباس عن القسورة فقال: هي جمع الرجال ألم تسمع

THALABI:v10p78/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p78/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p78/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses qaswara as the din or noise of people.
THALABI:v10p78/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله سبحانه فرت من قسورة قال: هي ركز الناس

THALABI:v10p78/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p78/r3.speaker: أبو المتوكل
THALABI:v10p78/r3.claim: Abu al-Mutawakkil says qaswara is the clamour of a crowd.
THALABI:v10p78/r3.anchor: عن أبي المتوكل في قوله سبحانه: فرت من قسورة قال: هو لغط القوم

THALABI:v10p78/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p78/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v10p78/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra interprets qaswara as a lion.

THALABI:v10p78/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p78/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p78/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says qaswara means lion in Arabic, while naming the Abyssinian, Persian, and Nabatean equivalents.
THALABI:v10p78/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس فرت من قسورة قال: هو بلسان العرب: الأسد، وبلسان الحبش: القسورة

THALABI:v10p78/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p78/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p78/r6.claim: An etymology derives qaswara from qasr, to overpower, since it subdues all wild beasts.
THALABI:v10p78/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو فعولة من القسر وهو القهر، سمي بذلك لأنه يقهر السباع كلها

THALABI:v10p78/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p78/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p78/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Ikrima, says qaswara means the hunters' ropes.
THALABI:v10p78/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى فرت من قسورة قال: من حبال الصيادين

THALABI:v10p78/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p78/r8.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v10p78/r8.claim: Ikrima also interprets qaswara as the darkness of the beginning of night, not the darkness at its end.
THALABI:v10p78/r8.anchor: وقال عكرمة: من ظلمة الليل، وقيل: هي سواد أول الليل ولا يقال لسواد آخر الليل

THALABI:v10p78/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p78/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v10p78/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says qaswara means strong men, and Arabs call anything large and powerful qasur or qaswara.
THALABI:v10p78/r9.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: أي من رجال أقوياء، وكل ضخم شديد عند العرب فهو قسور وقسورة

THALABI:v10p78/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p78/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p78/r10.claim: Labid's line illustrates qasawir as powerful men who come when called.
THALABI:v10p78/r10.anchor: قال لبيد: إذا ما هتفنا هتفة في ندينا … أتانا الرجال العائذون القساور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p398#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p398#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p398#2/r15.claim: The fleeing wild asses portray the deniers’ ignorance, since donkeys are among the most ignorant animals.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p398#2/r15.anchor: إثبات لجهالتهم لأن الحمر من جاهل الحيوان جدا

NAHHAS:v5p74/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p74/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p74/r6.claim: Qaswara follows the faʿūla pattern and derives from the root meaning to overpower or compel.
NAHHAS:v5p74/r6.anchor: فعولة من القسر قال أبو جعفر وقد ذكرنا ما قال أهل التفسير فيها

SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r10.claim: قسورة is explained as hunter, night darkness, or lion; another view says it means archers.
SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r10.anchor: والقسورة: قيل: الصائد. وقيل: ظلمة الليل. وقيل: الأسد، ومنه قول الشاعر

SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says he does not know قسورة to mean lion in Arabic; he interprets it as a company of men, while another view takes it as archers, citing Labid.
SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r11.anchor: إلا إن ابن عباس أنكره، وقال: لا أعرف القسورة: الأسد في لغة العرب

SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r12.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r12.claim: The clause فرت may describe حمر as an adjective, alongside مستنفرة, or may be circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:74:50/r12.anchor: والجملة من قوله " فرت " يجوز أن تكون صفة ل " حمر " مثل " مستنفرة "

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r3.speaker: أعرابي
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r3.claim: A Bedouin heard a reader use fatḥa and said a qaswara had pursued them; on hearing فرت من قسورة, he concluded that مستنفرة meant fleeing.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r4.claim: قسورة is explained as either archers or a lion.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r4.anchor: فالقسمورة الرماة والقسورة الأسد فأما قول

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r5.claim: In the cited verse, Imruʾ al-Qays uses قسورا for قسورة, dropping the final tāʾ marbūṭa and adding alif for the rhyme.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p356#3/r5.anchor: وعمرو بن درماء الهمام إذ مشى بذي شطب عضب كمشية قسورا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p332/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p332/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p332/r1.claim: Qatāda says the qaswara from which they flee means arrows.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p332/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ فرت من قسورة ﴾ قال قسورة النبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r8.speaker: محمد بن سلام
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Sallam recounts asking the eloquent Bedouin Abu Sarar al-Atawi about the image; after the Bedouin confirmed that it fled from a qaswara, he concluded mustanfira means fleeing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r8.anchor: وقال محمد بن سلام: سألت أبا سرار العتوي، وكان أعرابيا فصيحا، فقلت: كأنهم حمر ماذا مستنفرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو موسى الأشعري وقتادة وعكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Qatada, and Ikrima interpret qaswara as archers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأبو موسى الأشعري وقتادة وعكرمة: القسورة: الرماة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة وجمهور اللغويين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r10.claim: Another interpretation from Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayra, and most lexicographers is that qaswara means a lion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وأبو هريرة وجمهور من اللغويين: الأسد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r11.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r11.claim: Ibn Jubayr says qaswara means hunters, close in sense to archers and also attributed to Ibn Abbas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r11.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: رجال القنص، وهو قريب من القول الأول، وقاله ابن عباس أيضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r12.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r12.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi interprets qaswara as early night, so the asses flee darkness; Abū Ḥayyān adds that wild asses are exceptionally skittish and Arabs liken camels to them for speed and lightness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r12.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: القسورة أول الليل، والمعنى: فرت من ظلمة الليل، ولا شيء أشد نفارا من حمر الوحش

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r1.claim: Qaswara is on the faʿūla pattern from qasr, meaning overpowering and domination.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r1.anchor: وهي فعولة من القسر وهو القهر والغلبة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra explains qaswara as a lion; al-Ālūsī cites Ibn Jarir, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and others for this report.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r2.anchor: أي أسد وهي فعولة من القسر وهو القهر والغلبة وأخرج ذلك ابن جرير وعبد بن حميد وغيرهما عن أبي هريرة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says qaswara means lion in Arabic and is the word for lion in Ethiopian.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r3.anchor: وأخرجه ابن المنذر عن ابن عباس أيضا بيد أنه قال هو بلسان العرب الأسد وبلسان الحبشة قسورة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r4.claim: An alternative report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the pursuers as men who hunt with bows.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r4.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه أنها الرجال الرماة القنص

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة وابن جبير وعطاء بن أبي رباح
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Ibn Jubayr, and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ likewise explain qaswara as hunting archers.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r5.anchor: وروي نحوه عن مجاهد وعكرمة وابن جبير وعطاء بن أبي رباح

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r6.claim: A separate report from Ibn ʿAbbās takes qaswara to mean the noise or voices of people.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r6.anchor: وفي رواية عنه أخرجها ابن عيينة في تفسيره أنه ركز الناس أي أصواتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r7.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies qaswara as hunters’ ropes.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r9.speaker: ابن الأعرابي وثعلب
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r9.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Thaʿlab say qaswara is the beginning of night, so the asses flee the darkness.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي وثعلب القسورة أول الليل أي فرت من ظلمة الليل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r10.speaker: جمهور اللغويين
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r10.claim: The majority of lexicographers take qaswara to mean lion.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r11.claim: The disbelievers’ avoidance of the Qurʾān and its admonitions resembles startled wild asses fleeing in panic; the comparison also disparages their foolishness.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r11.anchor: فقد شبهوا في إعراضهم عن القرآن واستماع ما فيه من المواعظ وشرادهم عنه بحمر وحشية جدت في نفارها مما أفزعها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r12.claim: The ass comparison is a manifest reproach, like the image of a donkey carrying books, and may testify to their stupidity and lack of reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r12.anchor: وفي تشبيههم بالحمر مذمة ظاهرة وتهجين لحالهم بين كما في قوله سبحانه كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفارا أو شهادة عليهم بالبله وقلة العقل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r13.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r13.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads ḥumur with a still mīm.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r14.speaker: نافع وابن عامر والمفضل عن عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r14.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿĀṣim read mustanfira with fatḥa on fāʾ, meaning its fright made the asses flee.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r14.anchor: وقد قرأ نافع وابن عامر والمفضل عن عاصم مستنفرة بفتح الفاء أي اسنفرها فزعها من القسورة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r15.speaker: أبو سرار الغنوي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r15.claim: The eloquent Bedouin Abū Sarār’s exchange with Muḥammad ibn Sallām distinguishes the forms: the wording with kasra suits the asses fleeing, while fatḥa describes their being driven.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#2/r15.anchor: أبا سرار الغنوي وكان أعرابيا فصيحا فقلت كأنهم حمر ماذا فقال مسنفرة طردها قسورة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r5.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r5.claim: Mujāhid, Qatādah, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk identify qaswarah as archers, with no singular of the same form.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك: "القسورة": الرماة، لا واحد لها من لفظها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says hunters, as transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās via ʿAṭiyyah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هم القناص وهي رواية عطية عن ابن عباس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says strong men; Arabs call anything large and powerful qasūr or qaswarah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r7.anchor: كل ضخم شديد عند العرب: قسور وقسورة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r8.speaker: أبو المتوكل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r8.claim: Abū al-Mutawakkil says it is people's clamor and voices.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r8.anchor: وعن أبي المتوكل قال: هي لغط القوم وأصواتهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r9.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r9.claim: ʿIkrimah transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that it means hunters' ropes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r9.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: هي حبال الصيادين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة وعطاء والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r10.claim: They identify a lion: wild donkeys flee from it as unbelievers flee on hearing the Prophet recite Qurʾān.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r10.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: هي الأسد، وهو قول عطاء والكلبي، وذلك أن الحمر الوحشية إذا عاينت الأسد هربت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r11.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r11.claim: ʿIkrimah also says night darkness; the first darkness of night is called qaswarah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r11.anchor: قال عكرمة: هي ظلمة الليل، ويقال لسواد أول الليل قسورة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r2.claim: Qaswara means a lion; the form faʿūla derives from qasr, to overpower.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r2.anchor: أي أسد فعولة من القسر وهو القهر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r1.claim: Qaswara can mean a fierce lion, powerful in domination, or hunters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r1.anchor: أي أسد شديد القسر عظيم القهر فنشبت في حبائل سقر أو صيادين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r2.claim: Their flight is prompted by something terrifying; the image is of fleeing a lion and becoming caught in Hell’s snares or in hunters’ grasp.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r2.anchor: لا يكون إلا لسبب عظيم يتشوف إليه

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r4.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r4.claim: Abu Musa glosses qaswara as hunters who shoot arrows.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r4.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري في قوله: {فرت من قسورة} قال: هم الرماة رجال القنص

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas defines qaswara as men who hunt with bows.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: القسورة الرجال الرماة رجال القنص

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r6.claim: Abu Jamra proposes qaswara means a lion, but Ibn Abbas rejects that as Arabic usage and says it means a band of men.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r6.anchor: قلت لابن عباس قال: القسورة الأسد فقال: ما أعلمه بلغة أحد من العرب الأسد هم عصبة الرجال

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r7.claim: Ikrima compares the asses to wild asses fleeing from their archers.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة {كأنهم حمر مستنفرة فرت من قسورة} قال: وحشية فرت من رماتها

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r8.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says qaswara means hunters.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {فرت من قسورة} قال: القناص

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r9.claim: Mujahid defines qaswara as hunters or archers.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد {فرت من قسورة} قال: القناص الرماة

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r10.speaker: أبو مالك وعطاء بن أبي رباح
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r10.claim: Abu Malik and, in a matching report, Ata ibn Abi Rabah gloss qaswara as archers.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r10.anchor: عن أبي مالك قال: القسورة الرماة

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the asses as fleeing from hunters' ropes.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس {من قسورة} قال: من حبال الصيادين

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas also says qaswara is the people's noise or voices.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس {من قسورة} قال: هو ركز الناس يعني أصواتهم

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas also says qaswara means lion in Arabic; Abyssinian also uses qaswara for lion.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r14.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {من قسورة} قال: هو بلسان العرب الأسد وبلسان الحبشة قسورة

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r15.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r15.claim: Abu Hurayra says qaswara means a lion.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r15.anchor: عن أبي هريرة في قوله: {فرت من قسورة} قال: الأسد

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r1.speaker: أبو موسى الاشعري
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r1.claim: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari glosses qaswarah as archers, men who hunt.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r1.anchor: عن أبي موسى الاشعري في قوله : فرت من قسورة قال : هم الرماة رجال القنص .

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains qaswarah as archers, men who hunt.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : القسورة الرجال الرماه رجال القنص .

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r3.claim: In Abu Jamrah's report, Ibn Abbas calls qaswarah a lion, then says he does not know this as an Arab expression and describes lions as a band of men.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r3.anchor: عن أبي جمرة قال : قلت لابن عباس قال : القسورة الاسد . فقال : ما اعلمه بلغة أحد من العرب ، الاسد هم عصبة الرجال .

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the term is al-asad in Arabic and qaswarah in Abyssinian.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3385#3/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : من قسورة قال : هو بلسان العرب الاسد وبلسان الحبشة قسورة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r2.claim: The next passage expresses amazement at their persistence in rejecting reminders, following the statement that the Qur’an is a reminder for humankind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r2.anchor: تفريع للتعجيب من إصرارهم على الإعراض عن ما فيه تذكرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r6.claim: Their imagined rejection is likened to the flight of frightened wild asses, making an abstract state vivid through a sensory comparison.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r6.anchor: وشبهت حالة إعراضهم المتخيلة بحالة فرار حمر نافرة مما ينفرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r7.claim: Ḥumur here are wild donkeys, which startle and flee when they hear a hunter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r7.anchor: وهو الحمار الوحشي ، وهو شديد النفار إذا أحس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r8.claim: Labīd compares his mount’s speed to a wild animal pursued by a hunter; such flight imagery is common in pre-Islamic and Islamic Arabic poetry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r8.anchor: كما قال لبيد في تشبيه راحلته في سرعة سيرها بوحشية لحقها الصياد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r9.claim: The author notes this motif in the Muʿallaqāt of Ṭarafa, Labīd, and al-Ḥārith, in rajaz poetry by al-Ḥajjāj and his son, and in Dhū al-Rumma.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p328/r9.anchor: كما في معلقة طرفة ، ومعلقة لبيد ، ومعلقة الحارث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r5.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r5.claim: Most exegetes, including Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, and Mujāhid, take qaswara as a collective noun for archers, or as an irregular plural; this follows the familiar Arab simile.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد وغيرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة وزيد بن أسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r6.claim: Another transmitted view takes qaswara as a singular meaning lion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r6.anchor: وهذا مروي عن أبي هريرة وزيد بن أسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also glosses it as lion in Ethiopic; his differing statements may be verbal, since he denied that lion is the word’s original Arabic sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : إنه الأسد بالحبشية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r8.speaker: ابن السبكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r8.claim: Ibn al-Subkī lists qaswara among Qur’anic words from a language other than Arabic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r8.anchor: وقد عده ابن السبكي في الألفاظ الواردة في القرآن بغير لغة العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r9.speaker: ابن سيده
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r9.claim: Ibn Sīda says both qaswar and qaswara mean lion, with the latter grammatically feminine like Usāma.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r10.claim: If qaswara means lion, the simile is novel: their rejection mixes with terror inspired by the Qur’an’s menacing warnings, combining two representations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا فهو تشبيه مبتكر لحالة إعراض مخلوط برعب مما تضمنته قوارع القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r11.claim: Qaswara is chosen because it works for both proposed similes and preserves the verse ending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r11.anchor: هنا لصلاحيته للتشبيهين مع الرعاية على الفاصلة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو هريرة، زيد بن أسلم وابنه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r1.claim: The first view says qaswara is a lion, transmitted by Yusuf ibn Mihran from Ibn Abbas and also held by Abu Hurayra, Zayd ibn Aslam, and his son.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r1.anchor: أحدها أنه الأسد رواه يوسف بن مهران عن ابن عباس وبه قال أبو هريرة وزيد بن أسلم وابنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that wild asses flee when they see a lion, just as these polytheists flee when they hear the Prophet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس الحمر الوحشية إذا عاينت الأسد هربت منه فكذلك هؤلاء المشركون إذا سمعوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هربوا منه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r3.claim: Abu ʿUbayda and al-Zajjaj also take qaswara to mean a lion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r3.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب أبو عبيدة والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives qaswara from coercion or overpowering, since a lion overpowers other beasts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة كأنه من القسر والقهر فالأسد يقهر السباع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو موسى الأشعري، مجاهد، قتادة، الضحاك، مقاتل وابن كيسان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r5.claim: A second view identifies qaswara as archers; ʿAta transmits it from Ibn Abbas, and Abu Musa, Mujahid, Qatada, Dahhak, Muqatil, and Ibn Kaysan agree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r5.anchor: والثاني أن القسورة الرماة رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس وبه قال أبو موسى الأشعري ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك ومقاتل وابن كيسان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r6.claim: A third view, transmitted by ʿIkrima from Ibn Abbas, says qaswara means hunters’ ropes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r6.anchor: والثالث أن القسروة حبال الصيادين رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r7.claim: A fourth view, transmitted by Abu Hamza from Ibn Abbas, takes the term as a band of men; Abu Hamza was Nasr ibn Imran al-Dubai.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r7.anchor: والرابع أنهم عصب الرجال رواه أبو همزة عن ابن عباس واسم أبي حمزة نصر بن عمران الضبعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r8.claim: A fifth view, also reported from Ibn Abbas by ʿAta, glosses it as the people’s noise and sounds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r8.anchor: والخامس أنه ركز الناس وهذا في رواية عطاء أيضا عن ابن عباس وركز الناس حسهم وأصواتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r9.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r9.claim: A sixth view, attributed to ʿIkrima, says qaswara means darkness and night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r9.anchor: والسادس أنه الظلمة والليل قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p412#3/r10.claim: A seventh view, attributed to Qatada, says qaswara means arrows.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r1.claim: Their flight from truth resembles wild asses fleeing a predator or pursuer who wants to hunt them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r1.anchor: أي: كأنهم في نفارهم عن الحق، وإعراضهم عنه حمر من حمر الوحش إذا فرت ممن يريد صيدها من أسد،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم وعبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra, one report from Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Aslam, and his son identify qaswara as a lion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r2.anchor: قاله أبو هريرة، وابن عباس -في رواية-عنه وزيد بن أسلم، وابنه عبد الرحمن.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r3.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas, which Ibn Kathir says is the majority view, takes qaswara as an archer or hunter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r3.anchor: أو: رام، وهو رواية (3) عن ابن عباس، وهو قول الجمهور.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says qaswara means lion in Arabic, shīr in Persian, and awiya in Nabataean, with an Ethiopic name also given.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: الأسد، بالعربية، ويقال له بالحبشية: قسورة، وبالفارسية: شير (2)

JISHUMI:v10p7170/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r7.claim: Al-qaswara derives from seizing forcefully, as in qasara and qahara, both meaning overpower.
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r7.anchor: والقسورة: أصله الأخذ بشدة من: قسره يقسره قسرا نحو: قهره يقهره قهرا،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r5.claim: Al-qaswara can mean a band of archers who hunt wild asses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r5.anchor: جماعة الرماة الذين يتصيدونها . وقيل : الأسد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r6.claim: Another explanation takes al-qaswara to mean a lion; the word is on the faʿūla pattern from qasr, overpowering and subduing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r6.anchor: يقال : ليوث قساور وهي فعولة من القسر : وهو القهر والغلبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains al-qaswara as the clamor and voices of people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ركز الناس وأصواتهم . وعن عكرمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r8.speaker: عكرمة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r8.claim: ʿIkrima explains al-qaswara as the darkness of night.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r8.anchor: وعن عكرمة : ظلمة الليل ، شبههم في إعراضهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r9.claim: Their avoidance of Qur’an and admonition is likened to startled wild asses bolting; the comparison plainly censures their foolishness and lack of sense, like the donkey carrying books.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r9.anchor: شبههم في إعراضهم عن القرآن واستماع الذكر والموعظة وشرادهم عنه ، بحمر جدت في نفارها مما أفزعها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r10.claim: The vivid simile draws on the especially swift stampede of wild asses when startled, a standard Arab comparison for camels’ speed and flight from hunters at water.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r10.anchor: ولا ترى مثل نفار حمير الوحش واطرادها في العدو إذا رأبها رائب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p658/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p658/r3.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p658/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet promises ten good deeds for each person in Mecca who believed in Muhammad or disbelieved in him to whoever recites al-Muddaththir; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p658/r3.anchor: من قرأ سورة المدثر أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد من صدق بمحمد وكذب به بمكة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says qaswara means archers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r1.anchor: أن القسورة الرماة , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r2.claim: Al-Mawardi gives “hunter” or “game hunter” as another sense and cites a verse attributed to Ali as usage evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r2.anchor:
أنه القناص أي الصياد , ومنه قول علي :
يا ناس إني مثل قسورة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra says qaswara means lion.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, in a report transmitted by Yusuf ibn Mahran, says qaswara is the Abyssinian word for lion; al-Farazdaq's verse is cited as lexical evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r4.anchor:
روى يوسف بن مهران عن ابن عباس أنه الأسد بلسان الحبشة , قال الفرزدق :
إلى هاديات صعاب الرؤوس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r5.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas through Abu Hamza takes qaswara as a band or group of men.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r5.anchor: أنهم عصب من الرجال وجماعة , رواه أبو حمزة عن ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r6.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas through ʿAta takes qaswara as people's voices.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r6.anchor: أنه أصوات الناس , رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r7.claim: Qatada says qaswara means the noble or prominent men.

BURSEVI:v10p187/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p187/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p187/r3.claim: Qaswara means a lion, which wild asses flee intensely; haydara resembles it in form and sense, and qaswara derives from overpowering and subduing.
BURSEVI:v10p187/r3.anchor: أي من أسد لأن الوحشية إذا عاينت الأسد تهرب أشد الهرب

BURSEVI:v10p187/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p187/r4.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
BURSEVI:v10p187/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says qaswara is the Abyssinian word for lion; another view takes it as a band of hunters or archers.
BURSEVI:v10p187/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : القسورة هو الأسد بلسان الحبشة

BURSEVI:v10p187/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p187/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p187/r5.claim: Kashifi's Persian gloss lists lions, hunters, ropes or traps, archers, and various noises as things from which they flee.
BURSEVI:v10p187/r5.anchor: (وقال الكاشفي) : كريخنذ از شيريا از صياد ياريسمان دام يا مردم تيرانداز يا آوازهاى مختلف

BURSEVI:v10p187/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p187/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p187/r6.claim: Their rejection and flight from Quranic admonition resemble wild asses driven into frantic flight by what frightens them.
BURSEVI:v10p187/r6.anchor: شبهوا في أعراضهم عن القرآن واستماع ما فيه من المواعظ

NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r1.claim: “Fleeing from qaswara” is a circumstantial clause with qad understood.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r2.claim: Qaswara can mean archers or a lion; the word derives from qasr, overpowering and domination.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r2.anchor: والقسورة الرماة أو الأسد فعلة من القسر وهو القهر والغلبة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r3.claim: Their aversion to the Qurʾān and hearing the reminder is likened to wild asses in flight.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#10/r3.anchor: شبهوا في إعراضهم عن القرآن واستماع الذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r1.claim: Farrat means fled; the author first explains qaswara as archers who shoot at the animals.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فرت } أي نفرت وهربت { من قسورة } أي من رماة يرمونها.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r2.claim: Some philologists define qaswara as an archer, with qaswara as its plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r2.anchor: وقال بعض أهل اللغة: إن القسورة الرامي، وجمعه القسورة.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r3.claim: These authorities say qaswara refers to archers or hunters; the report is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas by ʿAta and from Abu Musa by Abu Dhabyan.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r3.anchor: وكذا قال سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وابن كيسان: القسورة: هم الرماة والصيادون،

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra and, in another report, Ibn Abbas say qaswara means a lion.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r4.anchor: وقيل: إنه الأسد قاله أبو هريرة وابن عباس أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r5.speaker: ابن عرفة
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r5.claim: Ibn ʿArafa derives the word from qasr, subjugation: the lion overpowers beasts, so wild asses flee it.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r5.anchor: ابن عرفة: من القسر بمعنى القهر أي إنه يقهر السباع، والحمر الوحشية تهرب من السباع.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r6.claim: Abu Jamra transmits Ibn Abbas's view that he does not know qaswara to mean lion in any Arab dialect; it means a group or band of men.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r6.anchor: وروى أبو جمرة عن ابن عباس قال: ما أعلم القسورة الأسد في لغة أحد من العرب، ولكنها عصب الرجال قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r7.claim: A quoted verse about a girl whose maternal uncles are jinn and people of the qaswara supports the meaning “men” or “group of men.”
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r7.anchor: قال: فالقسورة جمع الرجال، وأنشد: يا بنت كوني خيرة لخيره أخوالها الجن وأهل القسوره

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses qaswara as the gathering or sound of people.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r8.anchor: وعنه: ركز الناس أي حسهم وأصواتهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r9.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas interprets the phrase as fleeing from hunters' ropes.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r9.anchor: وعنه أيضا: «فرت من قسورة» أي من حبال الصيادين.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says qaswara means lion in Arabic, archers in Ethiopic, shir in Persian, and aria in Nabataean.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r10.anchor: وعنه أيضا: القسورة بلسان العرب: الأسد، وبلسان الحبشة: الرماة وبلسان فارس: شير،

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r11.speaker: ابن الأعرابي وعكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r11.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi and ʿIkrima say qaswara means the beginning of night or its first darkness, not the last darkness.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r11.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: القسورة: أول الليل أي فرت من ظلمة الليل. وقاله عكرمة أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r12.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r12.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says qaswara means strong men; in Arabic, anything strong is called qaswar or qaswara.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r12.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: من رجال أقوياء، وكل شديد عند العرب فهو قسورة وقسور.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r13.speaker: لبيد بن ربيعة
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r13.claim: Labid ibn Rabiʿa's verse about strong men rushing to their gathering witnesses qasawir as strong men.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:51/r13.anchor: وقال لبيد بن ربيعة: إذا ما هتفنا هتفة في ندينا أتانا الرجال العائدون القساور

RAZI-FULL:v30p186#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#3/r3.claim: Their aversion to the Qur'an is likened to frightened wild asses fleeing from a pursuer.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#3/r3.anchor: ثم شبههم في نفورهم عن القرآن بحمر نافرة فقال : ! 7 { كأنهم حمر مستنفرة * فرت من قسورة }

RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r5.speaker: أبو سوار الغنوي
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Sallam asked the eloquent Bedouin Abu Sawwar what kind of asses; he answered that they were mustanfira, driven by a qaswara, supporting the kasra reading.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r5.anchor: قال : سألت أبا سوار الغنوي ، وكان أعرابيا فصيحا

RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r6.claim: One proposed meaning of qaswara is a lion; the word is linked to qasr, subjugation, since the lion overpowers beasts.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r6.anchor: أنها الأسد يقال : ليوث قساور ، وهي فعولة من القسر وهو القهر

RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas compares idolaters fleeing Muhammad to wild asses fleeing when they see a lion.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الحمر الوحشية إذا عاينت الأسد هربت كذلك هؤلاء المشركين

RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says qaswara is the Ethiopian word for lion.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r8.anchor: ثم قال ابن عباس : القسورة ، هي الأسد بلسان الحبشة

RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r9.speaker: عكرمة
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r9.claim: Ikrima disagrees that this is the Ethiopian word for lion, saying that the Ethiopian word is ʿanbasa.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r9.anchor: وخالف عكرمة فقال : الأسد بلسان الحبشة ، عنبسة

RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r10.claim: Another view takes qaswara as the group of archers who hunt the asses.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r10.anchor: وثانيها : القسورة ، جماعة الرماة الذين يتصيدونها

RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r11.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r11.claim: Al-Azhari says qaswara is a collective name for archers with no singular of the same form.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r11.anchor: قال الأزهري : هو اسم جمع للرماة لا واحد له من جنسه

RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r12.claim: Other proposed meanings of qaswara are the press and voices of people, or the darkness of night.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r12.anchor: وثالثها : القسورة : ركز الناس وأصواتهم ورابعها : أنها ظلمة الليل

RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r13.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r13.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the comparison brands them foolish: no flight is like wild asses' frantic running when afraid.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186#4/r13.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : وفي تشبيههم بالحمر شهادة عليهم بالبله ، ولا ترى مثل نفار حمير الوحش

STUDYQURAN:74:51/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:51/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:51/r1.anchor: Lion translates qaswarah, an enigmatic word

STUDYQURAN:74:51/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:51/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:51/r2.claim: Other interpretations of qaswarah are hunting spears, arrows, or hunters.
STUDYQURAN:74:51/r2.anchor: also interpreted to mean “hunting spears,” “arrows,” or “hunters” (Q, Ṭ).

TAB-FULL:v23p455/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p455/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p455/r1.claim: The polytheists turn from the reminder like startled donkeys fleeing from a qaswara.
TAB-FULL:v23p455/r1.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندنا، أنهما قراءتان معروفتان، صحيحتا المعنى، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب

TAB-FULL:v23p456/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r1.claim: Al-Tabari notes disagreement over qaswara, glossed by some as archers and by others as hunters or a lion.
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {فرت من قسورة} [المدثر: 51] قال: الرماة

TAB-FULL:v23p456/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the qaswara from which the donkeys flee as archers.
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {فرت من قسورة} [المدثر: 51] قال: الرماة

TAB-FULL:v23p456/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r3.speaker: أبو موسى
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r3.claim: Abu Musa also says qaswara means archers.
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r3.anchor: عن أبي موسى، {فرت من قسورة} [المدثر: 51] قال: الرماة

TAB-FULL:v23p456/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r4.claim: Mujahid says qaswara means a band of hunting archers; he also reports that some glossed it as a lion and others as archers.
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {قسورة} [المدثر: 51] قال: عصبة قناص من الرماة

TAB-FULL:v23p456/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r5.claim: An unnamed view says qaswara means a lion, while another group takes it to mean archers.
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم في القسورة: هو الأسد، وبعضهم: الرماة

TAB-FULL:v23p456/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r6.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r6.claim: Ikrima says qaswara means archers; when someone claimed lion was its Abyssinian meaning, he replied that the Abyssinian word for lion is ʿanbasa.
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {فرت من قسورة} [المدثر: 51] قال: القسورة: الرماة، فقال رجل لعكرمة: هو الأسد بلسان الحبشة

TAB-FULL:v23p456/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r7.claim: Qatada identifies the qaswara as archers who hunt with bows.
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، {فرت من قسورة} [المدثر: 51] وهم الرماة القناص

TAB-FULL:v23p456/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r8.claim: Qatada also glosses qaswara as arrows.
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {فرت من قسورة} [المدثر: 51] قال: قسورة النبل

TAB-FULL:v23p456/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r9.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v23p456/r9.claim: Another unnamed group says the pursuers are hunters.

TAB-FULL:v23p458/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses qaswara as the men who hunt or shoot game.
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {فرت من قسورة} [المدثر: 51] يعني: رجال القنص

TAB-FULL:v23p458/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr also says qaswara means hunters.
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في هذه الآية {فرت من قسورة}

TAB-FULL:v23p458/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also understands qaswara as a band or gathering of men.
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r3.anchor: سئل ابن عباس عن القسورة، قال: جمع الرجال

TAB-FULL:v23p458/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r4.speaker: فلانة في الجاهلية
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r4.claim: A pre-Islamic woman's poem uses qaswara for a collective of men.
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r4.anchor: قالت فلانة في الجاهلية: يا بنت لؤي

TAB-FULL:v23p458/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains qaswara as people raising their voices.
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، {فرت من قسورة} [المدثر: 51] قال: ركز الناس أصواتهم

TAB-FULL:v23p458/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r6.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r6.claim: Sufyān links the reported meaning “voices” to rakz in 19:98, “sound.”
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r6.anchor: قال سفيان: {هل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا}

TAB-FULL:v23p458/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r7.claim: Abū Hurayra says qaswara means a lion.
TAB-FULL:v23p458/r7.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبي هريرة، {فرت من قسورة}

TAB-FULL:v23p460/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives multilingual equivalents for qaswara: lion in Arabic, shar in Persian, ariya in Nabataean, and qaswara in Ethiopian.
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس،؛ أنه سئل عن قوله: {فرت من قسورة}

TAB-FULL:v23p460/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies qaswara as a lion.
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم، في قول الله: {فرت من قسورة}

TAB-FULL:v23p460/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra's interpretation, transmitted again here, is that qaswara means a lion.

TAB-FULL:v23p460/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says qaswara means a lion.
TAB-FULL:v23p460/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فرت من قسورة}

TAB-FULL:v1p13/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p13/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p13/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says قسورة means lion in Arabic, shar in Persian, aryā in Nabataean, and qaswara in Abyssinian.
TAB-FULL:v1p13/r4.anchor: عن يوسف بن مهران، عن ابن عباس

TABATABAI:74:49-52/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r1.claim: After the preceding threat and promise, the passage presents as astonishing the rejection of the Qur'an's reminder and recoil from manifest truth: they should believe, yet seek individual revelation instead.
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r1.anchor: في معنى الاستنتاج مما تقدم من الوعيد والوعد أورد في صورة التعجب من إعراضهم عن تذكرة القرآن

TABATABAI:74:49-52/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r3.claim: The simile depicts their state as they turn away from the reminder: like wild asses fleeing from a predator or hunter.
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r3.anchor: تشبيه لهم من حيث حالهم في الإعراض عن التذكرة

TABATABAI:74:49-52/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r4.claim: Humur is the plural of donkey and here means wild asses; mustanfira means fleeing, while qaswara is explained as either a lion or a hunter.
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r4.anchor: والاستنفار بمعنى النفرة والقسورة الأسد والصائد

TABRISI:74:49-56/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:49-56/r3.speaker: عطاء والكلبي
TABRISI:74:49-56/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and al-Kalbī identify the qaswara as a lion.

TABRISI:74:49-56/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:49-56/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:74:49-56/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares unbelievers fleeing the Qurʾan when the Prophet recites to wild asses fleeing after seeing a lion.
TABRISI:74:49-56/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الحمر الوحشية إذا عاينت الأسد هربت منه

TABRISI:74:49-56/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:49-56/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك ومقاتل ومجاهد
TABRISI:74:49-56/r5.claim: An alternative view from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muqātil, and Mujāhid takes qaswara as archers or hunting men.
TABRISI:74:49-56/r5.anchor: القسورة الرماة ورجال القنص عن ابن عباس بخلاف والضحاك ومقاتل ومجاهد

TABRISI:74:49-56/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:49-56/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:74:49-56/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr identifies qaswara as hunters.
TABRISI:74:49-56/r6.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير هم القناص

FARRA:v3p205/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p205/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p205/r6.claim: One reported meaning of al-qaswara is archers.
FARRA:v3p205/r6.anchor: والقسورة يقال: إنها الرماة، وقال الكلبي بإسناده: هو الأسد.

FARRA:v3p205/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p205/r7.speaker: الكلبي
FARRA:v3p205/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says al-qaswara means a lion.
FARRA:v3p205/r7.anchor: والقسورة يقال: إنها الرماة، وقال الكلبي بإسناده: هو الأسد.

FARRA:v3p205/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p205/r8.speaker: عكرمة
FARRA:v3p205/r8.claim: When told that qaswara means “lion” in Ethiopic, Ikrima answers that it means archers, while the Ethiopic word for lion is ʿanbasa.
FARRA:v3p205/r8.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: قيل له: القسورة، الأسد بلسان الحبشة، فقال: القسورة، الرماة، والأسد بلسان الحبشة: عنبسة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda identifies qaswara as a lion.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r1.anchor: {فرت من قسورة} قال أبو عبيدة: هو الأسد (3) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba connects qaswara tentatively to qasr, meaning overpowering, since a lion overpowers other beasts.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r2.anchor: وكأنه من "القسر" وهو: القهر. والأسد يقهر السباع.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r3.speaker: بعض التفسير
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r3.claim: Some exegetical interpretation identifies qaswara as archers.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r4.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna transmits Ibn ʿAbbas's view that qaswara is the noise of people, meaning their sounds and voices.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#3/r4.anchor: وروى ابن عيينة (5) . أن ابن عباس قال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p457/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p457/r11.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p457/r11.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi prefers kasra on the fāʾ, since the next verse says that the asses fled, implying that they fled themselves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p457/r11.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: (الكسر في "مستنفرة" أولى، ألا ترى أنه: قال "فرت من قسورة"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p457/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p457/r12.speaker: أبو سوار الغنوي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p457/r12.claim: Asked by Muhammad ibn Sallam, the eloquent Bedouin Abu Sawwar called them mustanfira; after hearing that they fled from a qaswara, he confirmed that description.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p457/r12.anchor: محمد بن سلام قال: سألت أبا # سوار الغنوي (¬1)، وكان أعرابيا فصيحا، فقلت: كأنهم حمر ماذا؟ قال: مستنفرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r1.claim: The ones who fled are the asses.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in transmissions from ʿAta and al-Kalbi, explains qaswara as a lion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r2.anchor: فروى عن ابن عباس فيها أقوالا، قال في رواية عطاء (¬3)، (والكلبي (¬4)) (¬5): إنها الأسد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra specifies a black lion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r3.anchor: وهو قول: أبي هريرة (¬6)، قال هي: الأسد الأسود (¬7).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة، وابن الأعرابي، والمبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r4.claim: These lexicographers gloss qaswara as lion, from qasr, subjugating unwillingly; the lion is so named for overpowering predators.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة (¬8)، وابن الأعرابي (¬9)، ....... (والمبرد (¬1)) (¬2): القسورة الأسد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas compares polytheists fleeing Muhammad or his recitation to wild asses fleeing a lion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الحمر الوحشية إذا عاينت الأسد هربت منه، كذلك هؤلاء المشركون إذا رأوا محمدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r6.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية سليمان بن قتة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r6.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Sulayman ibn Qitta says qaswara means lion in the Ethiopian language.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r6.anchor: وقال في رواية سليمان (بن قتة) (¬4) هي: الأسد بلسان الحبشة (¬5) (¬6)، وخالف عكرمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r7.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r7.claim: Ikrima differs on the Ethiopian term, saying the lion is called ʿanbasa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r7.anchor: وخالف عكرمة فقال: الأسد بلسان الحبشة: عنبسة (¬7).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r8.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية سليم بن عبد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r8.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report glosses qaswara as archers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r8.anchor: وقال (¬8) في رواية سليم ....... (بن عبد (¬1)) (¬2): هم الرماة (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r9.speaker: مجاهد، وأبو موسى الأشعري، والضحاك، ومقاتل، وابن كيسان، وعكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r9.claim: Mujahid, Abu Musa al-Ashʿari, al-Dahhak, Muqatil, Ibn Kaysan, and Ikrima also say the word means archers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r9.anchor: وهو قول مجاهد (¬4)، وأبي موسى الأشعري (¬5)، والضحاك (¬6)، ومقاتل (¬7)، وابن كيسان (¬8)، وعكرمة (¬9)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r10.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، والحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r10.claim: A related view glosses qaswara as hunters; it is transmitted from Ibn Abbas through ʿAtiyya and held by Saʿid ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r10.anchor: وهذا معنى قول من قال في "القسورة": إنهم القناص (¬11). (وهو رواية # عطية عن ابن عباس (¬1))

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r11.speaker: الحجاج عن عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r11.claim: Al-Hajjaj transmits from ʿAta from Ibn Abbas that qaswara means archers, men of the hunt, combining the two glosses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r11.anchor: أن الحجاج روى (عن عطاء عن ابن عباس) في "القسورة": الرماة، رجال القنص (¬6)، فجمع بين اللفظين.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r12.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r12.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi cites an untransmitted view from Ikrima that qaswara is the darkness of night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r12.anchor: قال عكرمة: "من قسورة": من ظلمة الليل (¬10).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r13.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r13.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says qaswara means the beginning of night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r13.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: القسورة: أول الليل (¬11).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r15.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r15.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says qaswara means strong men.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p460/r15.anchor: وقال (زيد) (¬13) بن أسلم: القسورة: الرجال الأقوياء (¬14)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:49-56/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:49-56/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:49-56/r3.anchor: فرت من قسورة } أي: الأسد. وقيل: الرماة الصيادون.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:49-56/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:49-56/r4.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:49-56/r4.claim: An alternative says qaswarah means archers or hunters.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r1.claim: The simile portrays the disbelievers' response to the Prophet and his message as abnormally thoughtless, foolish, coarse, and indecorous.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r1.anchor: Burada yapılan benzetme, inkârcıların peygamber ve onun mesajı karşısında gösterdikleri tepkinin normal bir insandan beklenmeyecek kadar bilinçsiz, ahmakça, kaba ve edep dışı olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır.

ITQAN:v2p403/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p403/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p403/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says qaswara, the term for what the onagers flee, means “lion” in Ethiopian.
ITQAN:v2p403/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس قال الأسد يقال له بالحبشية قسورة

BURHAN:v1p288/r25.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p288/r25.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p288/r25.claim: Al-qaswara is listed as an Ethiopian word for a lion.

ITQAN:v4p470/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p470/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p470/r2.claim: Qaswara can mean hunter or lion; similarly, ʿasʿasa can mean night’s arrival or departure.
ITQAN:v4p470/r2.anchor: ومن التنازع الموجود عنهم ما يكون اللفظ فيه محتملا للأمرين
